rules.decision: Route a response with three or more unordered categories to a nominal or multinomial logistic-regression candidate rather than binary logistic regression.
conditions: Response has three or more observed or defined categories
Categories have no defensible natural order
rules.action: Classify the response as nominal multinomial and route to a nominal or multinomial logistic-regression candidate for later method-specific review.
warnings: Do not collapse categories to binary merely to fit the current runtime without a research-based reason.
Do not impose an artificial numeric order on nominal categories.
Methodome does not yet have source-backed model-specific selection and diagnostic rules sufficient for autonomous recommendation of this model family.

source_evidence.support: Penn State defines nominal logistic regression for categorical responses with three or more unordered levels.

rules.decision: Route a response with three or more naturally ordered categories to an ordinal logistic-regression candidate rather than treating category codes as a continuous outcome.
conditions: Response has three or more observed or defined categories
Categories have a defensible natural ordering
rules.action: Preserve the category ordering and route to an ordinal logistic-regression candidate for later model-specific review.
diagnostics: Codebook or instrument evidence supporting the order
warnings: Numeric category codes do not imply equal spacing between levels.
Do not treat an ordinal response as continuous solely because its categories are coded with numbers.
Model-specific ordinal-logistic assumptions are not yet sufficiently source-backed in the current corpus for autonomous recommendation.

source_evidence.support: Penn State defines ordinal logistic regression for responses with three or more naturally ordered categories and notes that ranked levels need not have equal intervals.
